macro_note.reason: Capped at 0.25, below the engine's 0.35 (RISK-OFF, score -1, VIX 36.9 intraday, 11.7% of universe above MA50, SPY -5.1% vs MA200, QQQ -10.2% vs MA200). Three sourced things the price gauge does not see: (1) the Fed is tightening into the drawdown - held 3.75-4.00% on Oct 28, minutes show confidence in a December hike, CME FedWatch ~95% for +25bp on Dec 9 (Kalshi 77-91%) with a January hike also being priced; Oct core CPI +0.3% m/m vs +0.2% expected; 10Y 5.085% / 30Y 5.426% on Nov 19 (10Y ~4.94-4.98% on Nov 20 on safe-haven bid) so the house 30Y>=5% gate is on. (2) Credit stress is concentrated exactly where the universe is long: CoreWeave 5Y CDS up to ~1,233bp on Nov 20, CCC spreads ~1,000bp (+500bp from 2026 lows per Vanguard), while the HY index OAS is only ~3.43% (Nov 17) - the index is hiding it, and a break above 4% would be the broadening signal. (3) VIX curve inverted (backwardation as of Nov 19 close; it was in contango Nov 13), i.e. the house term-structure gate is on. Event risk inside the holding window lands in a holiday-thinned tape: PCE + GDP Nov 25, payrolls Dec 4, FOMC Dec 9, CPI Dec 10. The driver is a trend change in the AI-capex leadership (three-plus weeks of selling since late Oct, S&P in correction, Nasdaq YTD gains erased) with shocks layered on top (Nvidia CEO resignation Nov 12, $68bn+ Anthropic IPO supply Nov 19 then a steep day-two fall), not a one-day shock, despite strong reported earnings (Q3 blended EPS growth 31.9%, NVDA beat and guided $130bn).
add_risk_when: Lift cap back to engine figure (stop overriding) when VIX front-month returns to contango (VIX < VIX3M) for 2 consecutive closes AND VIX closes below 28
HY index OAS stays below 4.0% and CoreWeave 5Y CDS retraces below ~1,000bp
QQQ closes back above MA50 with universe breadth above 40% (engine regime flips; trend basket re-enabled per PLAYBOOKS)
Dec 9 FOMC delivers the priced 25bp hike without signalling January (or holds) and 30Y closes below 5.0%
KOSPI reclaims 5,300 / stops making lower lows and BTC reclaims its MA50 (house 12a/12c confirmations)
cut_risk_when: Cut cap to 0.15: HY index OAS above 4.0% or CCC spreads above ~1,200bp (credit stress broadening beyond AI names)
Cut cap to 0.15: VIX closes above 40 with the curve still inverted, or SPY closes more than 8% below MA200
Cut cap to 0.15: Oct PCE (Nov 25) core at or above +0.4% m/m, or market prices a 50bp hike for Dec 9 above ~25%
30Y closes above 5.5% (new high in long yields while equities fall = no bond hedge)
A disorderly AI-credit event: CoreWeave or another neocloud/datacenter issuer misses a payment, pulls a financing or draws a covenant waiver
KOSPI closes below 4,700 or Hang Seng confirms bear market (>20% off Jan 29 peak) with BTC below $55,000

expected.assumptions: IC 0.05 on factor score, IC 0.1 on analyst views, ERP 5%; model estimate, not a forecast

analyst_notes.thesis: Fact: Q3 2026 revenue +39% to $24.4bn; FY2026 revenue guidance raised to $91-92bn from $85-87bn; oral GLP-1 Foundayo already at $184m quarterly sales; retatrutide Phase 3 positive. Forward P/E cited ~33x versus a 5-year average of ~40x. Inference: the only large-cap in scope with accelerating organic growth that is unrelated to oil or AI capex; quality is real, not an artefact.
analyst_notes.risks: Valuation: average analyst target cited ~$1,330-1,337 is below the $1,349.98 snapshot price, so upside depends on further estimate raises. Headline non-GAAP EPS guide was trimmed to $35.00-36.00 by ~$4.2bn acquired IPR&D charges. Zepbound realised prices falling; drug-pricing policy. Stock closed at a high of $1,443.50 on Nov 13 and is ~6% lower in the snapshot.

analyst_notes.thesis: Fact: Q3 2026 revenue $4.87bn (+19%) vs $4.75bn expected, gross booking value +21% to $27.7bn, nights booked +16% (about +13% excluding Reserve Now Pay Later); FY revenue growth outlook raised to high-teens, adjusted EBITDA margin ~36%, new $12bn buyback authorisation (about 12% of the $100.6bn market cap in the file). Net cash $4.9bn. Inference: growth is re-accelerating with a capital-return backstop at a ~5% FCF yield.
analyst_notes.risks: Management said Q3 was the peak of the pay-later net benefit, so Q4 nights growth guides lower (at least low-double-digit) as cancellations catch up; EPS was flattered by a $135m lower tax provision. Discretionary travel is exposed if the selloff and ~5% 10-year yields hit consumers. Figures from secondary coverage of the shareholder letter.

analyst_notes.thesis: Fact: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $4.23 vs ~$3.90 expected, FCF $19.1bn, $9.4bn returned in the quarter, $20bn buyback planned for 2027, Q4 dividend raised to $1.07; net debt $22.1bn. Energy Products earnings jumped to $9.1bn from $4.1bn while upstream fell to $7.3bn. Inference: the beat was a refining-margin windfall from the supply disruption; with crude down ~15% in November and margins likely to normalise, trailing growth and yield overstate forward earnings. Committed buyback and balance sheet limit downside.
analyst_notes.risks: Crude and crack spreads falling; shares fell ~4% on Nov 18. Upside if Middle East supply is disrupted again. Forward consensus not found.

analyst_notes.thesis: The capex-light hyperscaler: no AI build-out to fund, so the price-of-capital shock that is hitting the group does not touch it. FQ4 2026 (reported 2026-11-02) revenue $114.5B +12% vs 9-11% guidance, iPhone $57.6B +17.5%, December quarter guided to be the best revenue quarter in company history with iPhone Duo (on sale 2026-10-23) all incremental. Only AI-chain candidate above both MA50 and MA200.
analyst_notes.risks: Management flagged memory-cost pressure on margins and supply constraints; earnings yield 2.65% / P/S 10.4 (candidates file) is not cheap; AI exposure is as a consumer of others' models, not a seller - this is a quality/defensive view, not an AI-growth view.

analyst_notes.thesis: Best-funded AI franchise with AI revenue visible: FQ1 FY27 (reported 2026-10-28) Azure +48% to $33.2B, quarterly capex $45.2B but FCF still +$18.6B. CY2026 capex trimmed to ~$170B from $175B because third-party capacity slipped, not because demand fell; FY27 capex still guided up. Earnings yield 4.0%, operating margin 47% (candidates file). Self-funded, so it gains share if neoclouds cannot finance.
analyst_notes.risks: FCF down 27% y/y; exposure to OpenAI, whose funding round reportedly closed ~$11B against a $30B target (WSJ via secondary sources, early Nov 2026); below MA50; next catalyst not until late January.

analyst_notes.thesis: Fact: Q3 2026 (reported Oct 30) adjusted EPS $5.28, operating cash flow ~$16bn, net debt cut $7.8bn, buybacks ~$2.5bn; downstream earned ~$4.9bn on high refining margins. Inference: the +35% revenue / +180% net income growth and 8% FCF yield the engine rewards are peak-cycle numbers earned at ~$100+ Brent; with Brent now ~$92 and a forecast surplus, forward earnings are likely lower, so the stock is fairly priced rather than cheap. Balance sheet and payout are solid, which argues against an outright avoid.
analyst_notes.risks: Falling crude and refining margins; shares fell ~4% on Nov 18 with oil. Upside risk if Hormuz disruption returns. Forward consensus EPS not found.

analyst_notes.thesis: Fact: Q3 2026 revenue +6.7% to $22.9bn, adjusted EPS $1.69 vs $1.63 expected; FY2026 guidance raised to revenue ~$92.6bn, adjusted EPS ~$7.28 and adjusted FCF ~$6.1bn; Q4 guide above consensus. Inference: at $106.46 that is ~14.6x guided EPS (my arithmetic) with a ~7% FCF yield, estimates moving up and the deliberate Amazon volume reduction largely behind it - cheap, improving and not AI- or oil-beta.
analyst_notes.risks: US average daily volume still expected down y/y in Q4; GAAP EPS $1.37 after a $182m goodwill impairment and transformation costs; high diesel prices; peak-season execution; freight is cyclical if the selloff reaches the real economy. Dividend coverage not checked.

analyst_notes.thesis: The chokepoint with monthly hard data: October 2026 revenue NT$586.89B, +59.7% y/y and +14.7% m/m, a record and above the NT$560-570B analysts expected (reported 2026-11-10); Q4 guide US$52.3-54.3B. Operating margin 58% (candidates file). Stock is -22% 1m and 20% below MA200 on no company-specific bad news: this is de-rating, not an earnings downgrade.
analyst_notes.risks: Tighter export controls under the incoming Congress; NVDA-related probe spilling into China chip policy; any hyperscaler 2027 capex cut shows up here with a lag; still in a downtrend.

analyst_notes.thesis: Q3 2026 (reported 2026-10-14) record sales ~EUR11.7B, +~55% y/y, gross margin 57.5%, FY2026 sales guidance raised to EUR44-45B, and management says 2027-28 tool supply is short of demand. Orders are multi-year and placed by TSMC/memory makers, one step removed from AI-lab funding. -36% off high.
analyst_notes.risks: No longer publishes quarterly bookings, so order momentum is not verifiable; China exposure to tighter export controls; semicap is late-cycle if capex growth plateaus in 2027.

analyst_notes.thesis: Core ads business is strong (revenue +26% y/y, operating margin 33%, earnings yield 5.3% - candidates file) and the stock is the cheapest hyperscaler. But it is funding AI capex ($135-145B for 2026, Q3 capex $34.9B) with an equity raise of up to ~$95B announced 2026-10-26, including new non-voting Class C shares - the clearest case in the group of capex outrunning internal cash flow, with no external cloud revenue to monetise it. Fell 7% the day after results (2026-10-22).
analyst_notes.risks: Dilution and governance (non-voting class); no 2027 capex guide found; 17% below MA50 and below MA200 - one bad month from the knife filter.

analyst_notes.thesis: Fact: fiscal Q3 2027 reported Nov 19: revenue $188.8bn (+5.2%), adjusted operating income +5.5%, US e-commerce +23%, marketplace/fulfilment services +49%; FY guidance raised to net sales +4.9-5.2% and adjusted EPS $2.84-2.89. Inference: fresh beat-and-raise removes near-term earnings risk and the business gains share when consumers trade down; one of few names with positive 1-month return (+6%). Conviction capped by valuation: ~45x the guidance midpoint at $128.38 (my arithmetic).
analyst_notes.risks: Rich multiple with the 10-year near 5%; reported operating income +16% is flattered by a $700m PhonePe charge a year ago; management cited >$2bn of extra diesel/transport cost this year. Post-earnings share reaction not found.

analyst_notes.thesis: Freshest positive print in scope: FQ1 FY27 (reported 2026-11-18) revenue $3.45B +39% y/y, FY27 revenue guidance raised to $14.52-14.57B from $14.10-14.20B; lifted the whole security group on 2026-11-19. Security spend is not funded by the AI capex cycle and rises with AI adoption. Event risk is now behind it.
analyst_notes.risks: Headline growth includes acquired revenue (organic split not verified); P/S 24 (candidates file); below MA50.

analyst_notes.thesis: Fact: Q3 2026 operating profit fell 6% to $12.71bn (underwriting profit -43%, Geico pretax -45%) but beat the FactSet estimate; Berkshire repurchased $9.6bn of stock in Q3 plus ~$2bn in October, and held $356.9bn of cash at end-September. Inference: record buybacks signal management sees the shares below intrinsic value, and the cash pile both earns a high short rate and is optionality in a market where breadth above MA50 is 12%. Lowest-vol name in scope (15%).
analyst_notes.risks: Insurance margins deteriorating (Geico loss costs and ad spend); the +79% net income growth in the engine is investment mark-to-market, not operations. Data flag: market_cap in the candidates file ($0.8bn) is wrong, so any value metric for this row is unusable.

analyst_notes.thesis: Cleanest balance sheet in the infrastructure layer and the only AI Infrastructure name that survived the screen. Q3 2026 (reported 2026-11-03) revenue $3.66B +58.5% vs $3.3B guide, non-GAAP operating margin 49.1%; Q4 guided $3.9-4.0B vs ~$3.6B consensus; 2027 growth guided 38-40% (~$18.5B). Sells to the self-funded hyperscalers, not to levered neoclouds.
analyst_notes.risks: Hyperscaler customer concentration; 2027 guide assumes the capex plans hold; P/S 17.7; 13% below MA50.

analyst_notes.thesis: Fact: October retail-month net sales $24.50bn (+12.6%); first nine weeks of fiscal Q1 +12.8%; comps +7.3% excluding gasoline and FX (gas inflation added ~3.9 points to the reported 11.1%); digital +22.5%. Inference: operating momentum is excellent, but the file shows a 1.9% earnings yield (~53x trailing) with the 10-year Treasury near 5%, and the stock is 0.75% off its high and 12% above MA50 - it is being bought as a shelter, leaving little margin for error.
analyst_notes.risks: Multiple compression if yields rise further or the defensive bid unwinds; headline comps are inflated by fuel prices. Fiscal Q1 report inferred for Dec 10 (not company-confirmed).
